title: Reject invalid pump data and recover authority deliberately
equipment: Variable-speed booster pump with recirculation valve
physicalPurpose: Prevent invalid pressure, timing, quality, or configuration data from corrupting controller state or silently retaining automatic authority.
principalTechnique: Fail-closed controller guard with first-fault latching and qualified recovery
objective: Map each invalid input class to a deterministic fault, prove the invalid scan cannot update the PID, and restore Auto only after acknowledgement, valid evidence, and state reinitialization.

simplifications: Failure inputs are injected only in simulation; no physical pump is disturbed to create lesson evidence.
The station selects one declared safe recirculation output rather than teaching process-specific safety analysis for every possible pumping topology.
The runtime typed-I/O boundary rejects nonfinite values before a PLC scan; the station guard additionally rejects finite values outside physical ranges.

baseline.limitation: Without a guard, reversed output limits could reach configuration arithmetic or partially replace the active record.

change.decision: Reject the scan before any PID call, latch the first cause, command the safe output, and require acknowledgement, qualified data, reset, state initialization, and renewed Auto authority.

acceptance.window: first scan of each isolated fault injection
first renewed Auto scan after qualified reset

abortPredicates: Any physical-limit, freshness, timing, quality, deadline, or active-configuration predicate fails outside the declared injected case
The controller or Configure is called on an invalid scan
The fault-latched valve command differs from 30 percent
Auto receives authority on the reset scan
safety.restorationMode: Fault-latched 30 percent safe recirculation, then measured-state initialization and separately renewed Auto
safety.physicalApprovalRole: authorised pump-station control and process-safety engineer
simulationOnlyRestrictions: Do not inject stale data, bad timing, invalid parameters, or missed deadlines on a physical pump for training. A physical implementation requires an independently reviewed safe-state and protection topology.

video.viewerOutcome: Prove that an invalid scan cannot mutate the PID and execute an acknowledged, qualified, bumpless recovery.

learning.context: A running pump controller depends on trustworthy pressure, timing, quality, and configuration data on every scan.
learning.reason: Lesson 29 guaranteed coherent ordering only for valid values. Invalid values must be stopped before they can corrupt the same retained controller state.
theory: The runtime typed-I/O boundary rejects nonfinite values. The station guard rejects physically implausible finite values, stale or bad-quality measurements, invalid elapsed time, missed deadlines, and invalid configuration records.
A first-fault latch preserves the first actionable cause. Acknowledgement records operator awareness but does not clear the latch or restore authority.
This station chooses a 30 percent safe output instead of hold-last because retaining the last action may retain the action that caused a hazard.
Recovery requires three valid scans, acknowledgement, explicit reset, measured-state PID initialization, and a later renewed Auto request.
learning.workedPrediction: Reversed 80/20 percent limits produce code 5, zero configuration or PID calls, unchanged revision 0, and 30 percent output. Codes 1 through 4 identify range, stale, cycle-time, and deadline cases. Qualified reset and later Auto both retain 30 percent at zero error.
practicalPreparation: Verify SP, PV, physical ranges, sensor quality and age, measured cycle time, deadline input, candidate validity, first-fault code, latch, acknowledgement, recovery count, call flags, authority, output, and simulation label.
Restore 6 bar, 40 percent, revision 0, 100 ms timing, fresh good-quality data, and the same seed before each isolated injection.
learning.baseline: Inject each invalid class one at a time and retain the exact first scan. For the configuration case, use 80 percent minimum and 20 percent maximum.
learning.change: Correct the data without reset, acknowledge, gather three consecutive valid scans, request reset with Auto false, then issue a separate renewed Auto request on the following scan.
learning.comparison: Compare exact fault identity, invalid-scan state mutation, safe-output error, recovery qualification, reset acceptance, and renewed-Auto output step.
learning.validation: Require codes 1 through 5, zero invalid-scan mutations, 30 percent throughout the latch, exactly three valid scans before readiness, no clear on acknowledgement alone, and at most 0.001 percentage points on renewed Auto.
learning.explanation: Validity detection, safe action, operator acknowledgement, proof of recovery, state initialization, and authority are separate decisions. Combining them would let one signal silently clear a safety boundary.
learning.transfer: Apply the same layered guard to every controller-facing workflow. Lesson 31 uses only valid evidence to choose the minimum sufficient controller for each plant.
